primaryIssues: GET /api/cart/items: DB calls inside loop leading to N+1
Same as 10k plus unindexed foreign keys on order_items (will cause full scans)
Multiple critical checkout endpoints contain looped writes causing DB lock contention
No application-level cache for product listing + unbounded queries
Multiple N+1 patterns on checkout and cart will exhaust DB and cause failures
Unindexed FK columns on order_items and orders will lead to full table scans

findings.title: POST /api/checkout/create-order — N+1 writes inside loop and no transaction
findings.detail: traceFunction downstream for src/app/api/checkout/create-order/route.ts shows multiple DB writes inside a for loop: prisma.orderItem.update, prisma.orderItem.create, prisma.orderItem.delete (loopedDbCallCount: 3). No prisma.$transaction wrapper observed for these per-item writes, causing N+1 write pattern and risk of partial writes under failure.
findings.breaksAt: ~200 concurrent checkouts (depends on average items per order; could surface earlier)
findings.fix: Wrap all order mutations in a single transaction. Batch per-item operations using createMany/updateMany where possible. For stock updates, use single UPDATE queries or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE + batch update instead of per-item round-trips.

evidence.trace: traceFunction downstream: src/app/api/checkout/create-order/route.ts — looped DB calls: prisma.orderItem.update, prisma.orderItem.create, prisma.orderItem.delete (for-loop, loopedDbCallCount:3)

findings.title: POST /api/checkout/confirm-order — DB writes inside loop inside transaction (N+1)
findings.detail: traceFunction downstream for src/app/api/checkout/confirm-order/route.ts shows prisma.$transaction used but inside it repeated per-item updates occur: tx.order.update, tx.productColor.update, tx.product.update executed inside a for loop (loopedDbCallCount: 3). Long transactions with many statements cause locking and latency.
findings.breaksAt: ~500 concurrent confirmations (degrades earlier with larger orders)
findings.fix: Within the transaction, replace per-item queries with batched updateMany or single UPDATE statements affecting multiple rows. Minimize logic inside the transaction; offload non-critical updates to background jobs.

evidence.trace: traceFunction downstream: src/app/api/checkout/confirm-order/route.ts — prisma.$transaction with tx.* updates inside for-loop (loopedDbCallCount:3)

findings.title: POST /api/checkout/verify-payment — looped tx updates (N+1)
findings.detail: traceFunction downstream for src/app/api/checkout/verify-payment/route.ts shows prisma.order.findUnique then prisma.$transaction performing tx.order.update, tx.productColor.update, tx.product.update inside a for loop (loopedDbCallCount: 3). This duplicates confirm-order risks and can create long-running transactions.
findings.fix: Batch updates inside the transaction or move non-critical per-item work to background processing. Reduce number of statements and duration of transactions.

evidence.trace: traceFunction downstream: src/app/api/checkout/verify-payment/route.ts — findUnique then prisma.$transaction with per-item tx updates inside for-loop

findings.title: GET /api/products — unbounded findMany (no pagination)
findings.detail: src/app/api/products/route.ts executes prisma.product.findMany({ include: { colors }, orderBy: { createdAt: 'desc' } }) with no take/skip/cursor. This returns the whole products table and will grow linearly with catalog size leading to high memory and DB load.
findings.breaksAt: When products table grows (>=10k rows) or under moderate concurrent listing traffic (hundreds of requests)
findings.fix: Add pagination (cursor/limit) to product listing endpoints, return trimmed fields for list pages, and add caching (CDN or Redis) for high-traffic lists. Consider indexing createdAt if sorting by it often.

evidence.trace: file content: src/app/api/products/route.ts — prisma.product.findMany with include: { colors } and no pagination parameters

findings.title: GET /api/cart/items — DB findMany inside reduce/loop inside transaction (N+1)
findings.detail: traceFunction downstream for src/app/api/cart/items/route.ts shows use of prisma.$transaction and within that tx.cartItem.findMany appears inside a reduce/loop; multiple tx.* operations (findFirst, update, create, findMany) are used per-request indicating per-item DB work instead of single prefetch.
findings.breaksAt: ~300 concurrent cart fetches with medium cart sizes
findings.fix: Prefetch cart items with a single findMany(cartId) including required relations and compute totals in application memory. Avoid per-item DB calls; batch writes when needed inside transactions.

evidence.trace: traceFunction downstream: src/app/api/cart/items/route.ts — tx.cartItem.findMany inside reduce/loop and multiple tx.* calls

findings.title: OrderItem foreign keys are not indexed (orderId, productId)
findings.detail: getSchemaDefinitions for prisma/schema.prisma shows OrderItem model has orderId and productId foreign keys but no explicit @@index entries. Missing FK indexes will cause scans for common lookups (order → items, product → order_items) at scale.
findings.breaksAt: When order_items exceeds ~100k rows or with concurrent order processing (~100+ concurrent ops)
findings.fix: Add indexes on OrderItem.orderId and OrderItem.productId (e.g. @@index([orderId]), @@index([productId])) and run a migration. Add composite indexes for frequent multi-column filters if needed.

evidence.trace: prisma/schema.prisma: OrderItem model has orderId and productId without @@index definitions

findings.title: Order.userId has no index — queries by user may be slow
findings.detail: Schema shows Order.userId is a foreign key but not indexed. Queries for user order history or admin lookups by user will cause full scans on orders table when large.
findings.breaksAt: When orders table grows (>100k rows) or on moderate user-history traffic
findings.fix: Add an index on Order.userId (e.g. @@index([userId])). Consider indexing createdAt or orderNumber depending on query patterns.

evidence.trace: prisma/schema.prisma: Order model includes userId but no index defined

findings.title: Serverless Prisma usage — global singleton present and prisma-accelerate detected
findings.detail: src/lib/prisma.ts uses a global singleton for PrismaClient (good for serverless). checkConnectionPool detected @prisma/extension-accelerate in dependencies, indicating an external pooler. No explicit pool parameters (max/min/timeouts) are set in the repo.
findings.fix: Continue using the global singleton. Ensure prisma-accelerate or external pooler is configured for production; add connection timeouts and monitor connection metrics. Consider explicit pool configuration in environment if needed.

evidence.trace: file: src/lib/prisma.ts — global singleton for PrismaClient; getDependencies shows @prisma/extension-accelerate present

summary.topConcern: POST /api/checkout/create-order — multiple DB writes inside for...of loop without a transaction (N+1 + missing transaction)
summary.estimatedScaleCeiling: ~200 concurrent checkout requests before user-facing failures (likely 100-500 depending on average cart size and DB config)
